title: Wikipedia car example - criteria and subcriteria hierarchy
description: The Jones family car-buying example that serves as Wikipedia's standing worked illustration of AHP. This fixture covers the judgment matrices the article publishes in text form: the four criteria compared with respect to the goal, the four subcriteria of Cost, and the two subcriteria of Capacity. (The article's alternative-level judgments are published only as images and are not included.) Expected local and global priorities are derived with the principal-eigenvector method; the global priorities the article displays are recorded in source_reported, where they are compared with the derived values.

source.notes: Criteria judgments are stated in the article's prose; the Cost and Capacity subcriteria judgments are stated in a footnote ('Purchase Price 2 over Fuel Cost, 5 over Maintenance Cost, and 3 over Resale Value; Fuel Cost 2 over Maintenance Cost and 2 over Resale Value; Maintenance Cost -2 vs. Resale Value'; 'Cargo Capacity -5 vs. Passenger Capacity' - negative values meaning the left element is less important).

scale.name: saaty-1-9
scale.notes: Judgments on Saaty's fundamental 1-9 scale; reciprocals (e.g. 1/3) and intermediate or fractional values are valid entries. Matrix entries may be given as numbers or as fraction strings such as "1/3".

source_reported.explanation: The article displays global priorities of Purchase Price 0.246, Fuel Costs 0.127, Maintenance Costs 0.050, Resale Value 0.081, Safety 0.237, Style 0.042, Cargo Capacity 0.036, Passenger Capacity 0.181 (summing to 1.000). These differ from the exact principal-eigenvector synthesis by up to about 0.003 and agree closely with the column-normalization approximation (see the alternate values), which suggests the software used to prepare the article applied an approximate prioritization method. The article does not state which method was used. Neither set of values is wrong; they are the outputs of different documented prioritization methods applied to the same judgments.
